A video as a WebGPU external texture under HTML cards

The two cards below are HTML. The video frame behind them is a separate texture, and one shader pass draws all three: the cards are glass that bends and blurs the frame. Type in the field, press the buttons, change the effect and tap the picture. "Measure on this device" times each way of getting the frame and the cards to the GPU.

Frame 0

HTML over video

Show the code one pass over a video texture and two element textures, on three routes
  1. The markup. Two drawable cards and a <video> that is a child of the canvas but not of a drawn element.
  2. The CSS. The cards have no background. The shader draws it.
  3. The frame on WebGPU. importExternalTexture() first, then copyExternalImageToTexture().
  4. The WebGPU route. Upload each card with drawElementImageToTexture(), import the frame, draw.
  5. The render pass. The bind group is made again for each frame, because an external texture cannot be kept.
  6. The WGSL shader. texture_external and two texture_2d in one fragment shader.
  7. Where the cards go. The page computes each card's position. CSS left and top do not move a canvas child.
  8. Hit testing. updateElementGeometry() with a translation to where the shader draws the card.
  9. The WebGL 2 route.
  10. The WebGL uploads. texImage2D(video) and texElementSubImage2D().
  11. The GLSL shader.
  12. The 2D route. drawImage(video), drawElementImage(), filters and compositing.
  13. The measurement on WebGPU.

How it works

  • The canvas has three children. Two are drawable cards. The third is the <video>, which has no drawable ancestor, so it is never part of an element's picture.
  • On WebGPU, device.importExternalTexture({ source: video }) gives the current frame as a GPUExternalTexture with no copy. queue.drawElementImageToTexture() puts each card in an rgba8unorm texture. One fragment shader samples the frame with textureSampleBaseClampToEdge() and the cards with textureSampleLevel().
  • If the import fails, the frame is copied with queue.copyExternalImageToTexture() and the same shader is compiled with texture_2d<f32> for the video.
  • On WebGL 2 the frame comes from texImage2D(video) and the cards from texElementSubImage2D(). On a 2D canvas the page uses drawImage(video), drawElementImage(), ctx.filter and compositing modes. The 2D route has no ripple.
  • The page tries WebGPU, then WebGL 2, then 2D. The line under the picture names the route in use and gives the reason when it is not WebGPU.
  • A shader draw does not place an element for hit testing. CSS left and top do not move a canvas child either. The page keeps each card's position, gives it to the shader as a rectangle, and gives it to updateElementGeometry() as a translation. It then toggles an attribute on the card.
  • The measurement compares this arrangement with the one /video/ and /overlay/ use, where the video is a child of the drawn element and one upload carries the frame and the HTML together.

Each check builds its own small canvas in a corner of the window. The WebGPU checks draw into a texture and read it back, so they also run on a software adapter. The picture above is not touched.

Findings

From Chromium 157 headless with a software WebGPU adapter (SwiftShader) and software video decoding, 2026-11-21. The rows above say what your browser does.

  • Works: the pass itself. One WebGPU render pass samples a video texture and two element textures. The frame number in the composed picture and the colours of the cards were read back from the target texture.
  • Fails here: importExternalTexture(). With the software adapter it throws "Failed to import texture from video" for a <video> and for a VideoFrame. copyExternalImageToTexture(video) also throws in Chromium 157 with this adapter. createImageBitmap(video) followed by copyExternalImageToTexture(bitmap) works, and the checks fall back to it. So the texture_external shader variant compiled here but did not draw. The first, third and eighth checks answer this on a device with a real GPU.
  • Works: the video inside the element. An element that contains a playing <video> uploads with drawElementImageToTexture() and its texture holds a frame.
  • Works: the same picture on WebGL 2. The GLSL and WGSL shaders were compared on a paused frame for all three effects. The differences are in the fifth check.
  • Needed: a translation in canvasTransform. A canvas child with left: 200px; top: 100px has its box at the canvas origin, and percentages in left, right and bottom gave a box 0 px wide. With an identity matrix the card is hit tested at the origin. new DOMMatrix().translate(200, 100), in CSS pixels, puts the hit box where the shader draws the card.
  • Needed: multiply by alpha in the shader. In these textures a box with rgb(200 100 50 / .5) is stored as 199, 100, 50 with alpha 0.5, on WebGPU and on WebGL 2. Adding the texture's colour to the frame without multiplying it turned every translucent control white.
  • Refused: an element as an external texture. importExternalTexture({ source: element }) throws a TypeError. An element reaches WebGPU only through the copy in drawElementImageToTexture().
  • Not verified here: WebGPU on screen, importExternalTexture() with a hardware decoder, whether the external texture expires, and every timing on a real GPU. The "Measure on this device" button and the live checks report these on the device that opens the page.
